Here’s a quick‑look guide to what most food writers, critics, and locals agree are the *best* places to get authentic, fresh sushi in Los Angeles—plus a few “must‑try” spots depending on your vibe: | Rank | Restaurant | Address & Neighborhood | Why It Stands Out | |------|------------|------------------------|-------------------| | **1** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 W Olympic Blvd – Koreatown | • Consistently tops local lists.
• Classic Edomae-style nigiri from a single chef who runs it himself.
• Freshness is king—daily deliveries from Japan.
• Prices moderate (~$12–15 per plate) and you’ll see the fish before ordering. | | **2** | **Sugarfish** | Multiple locations (West Hollywood, Downtown, Santa Monica) | • Known for its “no‑wait” system: order online → pick up within minutes.
• Focuses on simplicity: hand‑rolled rolls, sashimi, and a small menu that never changes.
• Great for casual dining or takeout. | | **3** | **Matsu** | 1225 E Cedar Ave – Silver Lake | • A hidden gem run by Chef Matsuhiro Kondo.
• Combines traditional techniques with seasonal California ingredients.
• Small plates feel like a tasting menu. | | **4** | **Yamashita** | 1209 Beverly Dr – Beverly Hills | • Upscale setting with a view of the city skyline.
• Offers both classic nigiri and creative fusion pieces.
• Excellent omakase experience (reserve well ahead!). | | **5** | **Tetsuya’s** | 200 Fifth Avenue – Mid-Wilshire | • Awarded one Michelin star in 2018.
• Japanese‑French hybrid dishes, including signature tuna tartare.
• Ideal for special occasions. | ### Quick Tips When Choosing Your Spot | Question | What to Look For | |----------|------------------| | **Freshness** | Ask about delivery times from Tokyo/Osaka. Chefs who keep their own fish tanks usually score higher. | | **Omakase Availability** | If you’re serious about trying everything, look for a place offering a set course dinner. | | **Price Range** | Traditional sushi ranges $10–20 per plate; omakase can hit $80+ per person. | | **Atmosphere** | Some diners prefer a bustling counter, others a quiet private room. | | **Reservations** | High‑end spots fill fast—book months in advance via phone or website. | #### Bonus Picks (If You Want Something Different) - **Umi** (Mid-City): Contemporary takes on sushi + great sake selection. - **Shin Soba** (Hollywood): Authentic soba noodles plus simple sushi rolls. - **Izakaya Yokocho** (Downtown): Casual izakaya vibes with plenty of small plates—including mini-sushi bowls. --- **How to Verify Current Status** Because openings change quickly: 1. Check each restaurant’s official site or Instagram for latest hours. 2. Read recent Yelp / TripAdvisor reviews (last 30 days). 3. Call ahead if you plan to dine during peak hours or book a table. Enjoy exploring L.A.’s vibrant sushi scene! 🍣
